Name: Basílica de Nuestra Señora del Pilar
Tips: Enormous Baroque basilica on the Ebro — Spain's most visited pilgrimage site. Free, open daily ~06:45–20:30 straight through siesta. Goya dome frescoes, Santa Capilla, 1936 unexploded bombs. Tower lift €6 (€4 youth), Mon–Thu 10:30–14:30 and 16–20, LAST LIFT ~19:30. Sunset (20:37 Aug 31) is from Puente de Piedra.

Name: La Aljafería Palace
Address: C/ de los Diputados s/n Zaragoza
Tips: 11th-century Moorish palace comparable to the Alhambra but almost no crowds. Islamic filigree arches, oratory mihrab, Catholic Monarchs' throne room. Open daily 10:00–18:00 (2026). Allow 1.5–2 hours. Book timed entry at tickets.aljaferia.es — capacity limited.

Name: La Seo Cathedral (Catedral del Salvador)
Tips: Built over a Roman forum and Moorish mosque. Mudéjar north wall is one of the finest in Spain; world-class Flemish tapestry museum included. OPEN MONDAYS: Mon–Sat 10–14:30 and 16–20 (last entry ~19:15). Cathedral + Pilar tower combo €12 (€9 youth) saves €4.

Name: Museo del Foro de Caesaraugusta
Tips: Excavated Roman forum preserved underground with excellent audiovisuals. Cool, uncrowded, genuinely fascinating. CLOSED MONDAYS — go Tue: 10–14 and 17–21. The €7 Roman-route combo only pays if you visit 2+ of the 4 museums.

Name: Puente de Piedra
Tips: 15th-century stone bridge over the Ebro — walk to the middle at dusk for the classic view of El Pilar's tiled domes reflected in the river. Sunset Aug 31 is 20:37; floodlights and blue hour to ~21:10. North-bank promenade gives the wider angle.

Name: Plaza del Pilar (Plaza de Nuestra Señora del Pilar)
Address: Plaza de Nuestra Señora del Pilar Zaragoza
Tips: The full scale of the basilica from the square is extraordinary — 156m long. Best seen in daylight. Links El Pilar and La Seo; Goya statue and Fuente de la Hispanidad along the way.

Name: Mercado Central de Zaragoza
Tips: 1903 Modernist iron market with stained-glass roof, beside the Roman walls. Stalls run Mon–Sat ~09:00–14:00 (plus weekday evenings); central tapas stands. Catch it alive before 14:00 — ideal Tue ~12:20 en route from the Aljafería.

Name: Teatro de Caesaraugusta
Tips: 6,000-seat Roman theatre ruin in the middle of the old town, visible free from the perimeter walkway anytime. Museum on the municipal schedule (closed Mondays). A free 10-minute wow 5 min south of Casa Lac.

Name: La Lonja
Tips: 1540s Renaissance merchant exchange — Aragón's finest civil Renaissance building. Interior opens only when an exhibition is on (closed Mon); the facade alone is worth the 2-minute detour between the cathedrals.

Name: Patio de la Infanta
Address: C/ San Ignacio de Loyola 16 Zaragoza
Tips: Spectacular 1550s Renaissance courtyard inside the Ibercaja HQ. Currently hosts Goya. Interludio — the Museo Goya collection while that museum is closed for expansion (until ~Oct 2026). Hours/price unverified — check before going.

Name: Museo Pablo Gargallo
Tips: Aragón's great modernist sculptor in a Renaissance palace. CLOSED MONDAYS; Tue–Sat 10–14 and 17–21, Sun 10–14:30. Siesta gap makes it hard on our Tuesday — future-trip item.

Name: Alma Mater Museum
Tips: Diocesan museum in the old bishops' palace next to La Seo — Renaissance rooms, sacred art, Ebro views. CLOSED MONDAYS; Tue–Sat 10–14 and 17–20, Sun 10–14.

Name: EMOZ Museo del Origami
Address: Centro de Historias, Plaza San Agustín 2 Zaragoza
Tips: One of the world's few origami museums, 5 min from the apartment. Closed Mondays; Tue–Sat split hours — verify. Great teen-pleaser or rainy-day swap.

Name: Iglesia de San Pablo
Cost Range: Free exterior (guided interior small fee — verify)
Tips: Zaragoza's third great church — 14th-century UNESCO Mudéjar octagonal tower. Interior opens limited guided hours; the tower reads best from Calle San Pablo.

Name: Iglesia de la Magdalena
Tips: Mudéjar tower two blocks from the apartment — the family's nightly landmark home. Open around Mass times; tower visible anytime.

Name: Basílica de Santa Engracia
Tips: Plateresque portal and a crypt with 4th-century early-Christian Roman sarcophagi. Open around Mass times — verify. 10 min south of the Pilar.

Name: Murallas Romanas y Augusto
Tips: Surviving stretch of 1st-century Roman walls with the bronze Caesar Augustus statue beside the Mercado Central. Zaragoza = Caesaraugusta, named with Augustus's full name. Quick photo stop.

Name: Calle Alfonso I
Tips: The 19th-century straight-shot street that frames El Pilar's domes — Zaragoza's daylight postcard view. Stroll it Tue afternoon; Fantoba is one street over on Don Jaime I.
